INSPECT BRIDGE EVIDENCE

What crossed the gap?

A certificate is a signed statement about a proposal. It moves information, not money.

The receiver will check the certificate against its configured foreign network.

A relayer delivers evidence. It does not decide what another network trusts.

Preparing fresh local state
01 / INDEPENDENT

Separate networks.

Each side has its own test keys and local certificate state. A certificate from the wrong network fails verification.

02 / DELIVERED

Evidence travels.

The relay carries encoded evidence across the gap. Pause it and the source can continue while certificates wait.

03 / VERIFIED

Trust has a check.

Nunchi’s verification and latest-view rules decide whether a certificate is accepted, rejected or already out of date.

Threshold signatures verify the group’s certificate. The displayed signing-share indices describe this local fixture; they are not third-party evidence of individual validator participation.

What’s powered by the SDK?+

NUNCHI BRIDGE

Verify, then admit.

The original BridgeActor::verify_payload and submit method bodies are extracted unchanged from the pinned SDK source and compiled through a synchronous browser adapter. They check the foreign certificate and compare its view to the latest accepted view.

DKG TYPES / COMMONWARE CRYPTOGRAPHY

Real certificates. Test setup.

The same threshold Scheme and Finalization types used by Nunchi DKG sign three fixture shares, assemble a BLS12-381 certificate and verify it with original Commonware code. The public test setup supplies the shares; a distributed DKG ceremony is not run here.

THE APPLICATION

Make the flow visible.

The application supplies the two local network models, synthetic proposal data, relay queue, playback, 3D islands and inspector. Authority, Chain, RPC, Mempool and node processes are not executed in this browser example.

Why would a developer build this?+

Use external chain information.

An application may need to react to what a separate network finalized. A signed certificate provides evidence to check against a configured foreign network.

Reuse the hard primitives.

Developers can compose existing certificate verification, encoding and bridge admission logic with their own chain runtime, relayer and business rules.

Define the trust boundary.

The application still chooses the foreign network and how to act on accepted information. This example demonstrates certificate verification, not a universal token bridge or an arbitrary claim about another chain’s state.

Simulation Assumptions & SDK Details+

What runs here

SDK 2026.9.0-alpha.1, commit eea35ced709f68c15d6fbc8bcc754696a7e44374; Commonware 2026.9.0. Two independent local test committees with four shares each. Certificate generation, cryptographic verification and latest-view admission run newly in browser WebAssembly.

Reset creates fresh session-derived test keys and empty state. These are public deterministic demo identities.

What “accepted” means

The certificate passed the receiver’s configured foreign-network verification and had a newer view than its cache. The accepted view updates local session memory. A valid repeat or older view is stale.

Chain heights are fixture proposal counters, not observed node heights. Synthetic block payloads are hashed and signed. Consensus networking, actual finality, QMDB inclusion/state-root proofs, epoch/key rotation and persistent storage are outside this demo.

Execution boundary

The browser adapter executes the original BridgeActor verification/admission bodies without spawning its async actor. Full BridgeExtension block integration is not executed. Original source hashes, adapter source and WASM fingerprints are provided.

No asset transfer, swap, external chain, public-network settlement, or live validator network is deployed. 256 certificates per local session. Export verification checks the included local command replay, not historical completeness.

Build with Nunchi+

These excerpts come from this implementation. Session, BridgeCore and BridgeNetwork are application adapters. The original SDK BridgeActor method bodies are compiled unchanged.

Initialize two separate test committees and receivers

 fn new(id: &str) -> Result<Self,String> {
    if id.is_empty() || id.len()>128 { return Err("Session ID must contain 1–128 characters.".into()); }
    let a=fixture(id,0); let b=fixture(id,1);
    let receiver_a=BridgeCore{foreign_network:b.verifier.clone(),state:State{latest:None}};
    let receiver_b=BridgeCore{foreign_network:a.verifier.clone(),state:State{latest:None}};
    Ok(Self{id:id.into(),networks:vec![Network{schemes:a.schemes,participants:a.participants,height:0,latest:None,receiver:receiver_a},Network{schemes:b.schemes,participants:b.participants,height:0,latest:None,receiver:receiver_b}],rng:StdRng::from_seed(seed(id.as_bytes())),records:vec![],accepted:vec![]})
 }

Assemble a source finalization certificate

 fn produce(&mut self, index: usize) -> Result<Value,String> {
    if self.records.len()>=256 {return Err("Session contains 256 certificates. Reset to create a fresh session.".into());}
    let network=&mut self.networks[index]; let height=network.height+1;
    let block=json!({"format":"bridge-lab/synthetic-block/1","session_id":self.id,"network":index,"height":height,"parent_payload":network.latest.as_ref().map(|f|encoded(&f.proposal.payload)),"work":"Local test proposal; not a deployed node block"});
    let bytes=serde_json::to_vec(&block).unwrap();
    let proposal=Proposal::new(Round::new(Epoch::zero(),View::new(height)),View::new(height-1),Sha256::hash(&[&bytes]));
    let votes:Vec<_>=network.schemes.iter().take(3).map(|s|Finalize::sign(s,proposal.clone()).unwrap()).collect();
    let finalization=CFinalization::from_finalizes(&network.schemes[0],non_empty![@votes.iter()],&Sequential).map_err(|e|format!("Certificate assembly failed: {e:?}"))?;
    let valid=finalization.verify(&mut self.rng,&network.schemes[0],&Sequential);
    if !valid {return Err("New fixture certificate did not verify.".into());}
    let proof=encoded(&finalization); let id=encoded(&Sha256::hash(&[proof.as_bytes()]));
    let record=json!({"id":id,"source_index":index,"destination_index":1-index,"height":height,"view":finalization.view().get(),"epoch":0,"payload_digest":encoded(&finalization.proposal.payload),"certificate_hex":proof,"certificate_bytes":finalization.encode().len(),"synthetic_block":block,"generated_by":"Commonware Finalize::sign + Finalization::from_finalizes, matching Nunchi Bridge tests","source_verified":valid,"fixture_signers":[0,1,2],"threshold":"3 of 4 public test shares"});
    network.height=height;network.latest=Some(finalization);self.records.push(record.clone());Ok(record)
 }

The original SDK verification and admission rules

    fn verify_payload<R>(&self, rng: &mut R, payload: &BridgePayload) -> bool
    where
        R: CryptoRng + Rng,
    {
        let Some(finalization) = payload else {
            return true;
        };
        finalization.verify(rng, &self.foreign_network, &Sequential)
    }

    fn submit<R>(&mut self, rng: &mut R, finalization: Finalization) -> SubmitResult
    where
        R: CryptoRng + Rng,
    {
        if !self.verify_payload(rng, &Some(finalization.clone())) {
            return SubmitResult::Rejected;
        }

        let replace = match &self.state.latest {
            Some(current) => finalization.view() > current.view(),
            None => true,
        };
        if replace {
            self.state.latest = Some(finalization);
            SubmitResult::Updated
        } else {
            SubmitResult::Stale
        }
    }

Relay the encoded certificate and read the result

 submit(cert=this.selected,{tamper=false,destination=cert?.destination_index}={}){if(!cert)throw Error('Create a certificate first.');const {verification}=this.perform('submit',{destination_index:destination,certificate_hex:cert.certificate_hex,tamper});this.result=verification;this.queue=this.queue.filter(item=>item.id!==cert.id);this.log(verification.result==='updated'?'Foreign certificate accepted':verification.result==='stale'?'Valid certificate is stale':'Evidence rejected',verification.error||'Latest foreign certificate view: '+verification.accepted_after,cert);return verification;}
